title: Troubleshoot bag-out stoppage with abnormal AGV or task sequencing
user_facing_summary: Use when bag-out stops or progresses only partially and the site reports that an AGV is not moving, robots are out of sequence, a pair is not exchanging, or a related HMI shows a fault.
playbook_goal: Determine whether an observable AGV, pairing, sequence, tote, or task condition is preventing bag-out from progressing; guide authorized recovery; and confirm that robots and bag-out operation return to a stable state.
observed_entry_symptoms: Bag-out stops after sorting or does not progress to completion.
The site must manually bag out.
One or more AGVs or robots are not moving for an extended period.
The site reports a robot out of sequence or out of position.
Bag-out starts after an AGV-pair change but stops again.
A hospital-area HMI reports a fault or a stuck task is visible there.
negative_or_absent_signals: No confirmed single failed robot, task, tote, or root cause is established in the incident.
No confirmed stack-light fault was reported during at least one bag-out observation.
The exact decisive recovery action is not isolated in the source.
support_user_language_examples: Hospital HMI is showing a fault
There may be a stuck task
tentative_internal_patterns: Possible AGV sequence, pairing, roster, or position inconsistency
Possible robot task or command remaining stuck
Possible tote or hospital-workflow state mismatch
Possible AGV availability or low-battery interruption
internal_pattern_notes: These are tentative patterns extracted from the incident and must not be treated as confirmed diagnosis or required entry criteria. The source reports a suspected robot out-of-sequence condition, an AGV that did not move for three hours, a tote read in an unexpected location, a hospital HMI fault, and a stuck task visible on that HMI.
separability_reason: The incident evidence supports one end-to-end troubleshooting objective rather than multiple independently reusable flows. AGV inactivity, pair replacement, HMI fault, tote identification, and stuck-task investigation all relate to restoring the same bag-out workflow.
confidence_reason: The incident provides clear entry symptoms, named diagnostic surfaces, high-level recovery actions, and a successful validation outcome. Confidence is reduced because the exact failed component and decisive recovery action are not isolated, several OCR excerpts are ambiguous, and the HMI location wording conflicts with the authoritative ingestion site metadata.

nodes.title: Confirm bag-out stoppage and affected operational pattern
nodes.intent: Confirm whether bag-out is stalled or only partially progressing and whether the observable pattern includes AGV inactivity, sequence or pairing concerns, or a related HMI fault.
nodes.goal: Confirm whether bag-out is stalled or only partially progressing and whether the observable pattern includes AGV inactivity, sequence or pairing concerns, or a related HMI fault.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected bag-out flow is stopped or only partially progressing, whether manual bagging is being used, whether AGVs are actively routing to the affected workflow, and whether the issue began with a robot, pair, tote, or HMI observation. In RMS, check the fleet activity or status view for the affected operational area without relying on incident-specific robot identifiers.
nodes.source_supported_description: The case subject and site messages describe a bag-out stoppage after sorting, manual bagging, and a robot believed to be out of sequence. The RMS artifact and related message report an AGV that did not move for three hours.

In RMS, check the fleet activity or status view for the affected operational area without relying on incident-specific robot identifiers.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site/operator observes the bag-out workflow and reports whether it is stopped, partially complete, or progressing normally; the operator or L1 support checks the RMS activity/status view when available. Unhealthy signals are bag-out not progressing, manual bagging required, or an AGV with prolonged inactivity. Healthy signal is normal bag-out progression with active AGV movement. Inconclusive means the current bag-out state, affected area, or robot behavior cannot be observed.
